D: A boy genius and his brother's gentle healthcare robot form a team to find out who caused a tragedy.
P: Serve the snacks when Aunt Cass brings out her hot wings.
S: Aunt Cass and her famous spicy wings
Chicken wings baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in a sticky glaze of gochujang, honey, garlic and soy.
Lucky Cat Café pork belly bao

Pork belly braised in soy, ginger and star anise until meltingly soft, sliced into steamed bao with hoisin, cucumber, spring onion and peanuts. Cut 800g pork belly into 3 thick strips and simmer in 100ml soy, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 4 slices ginger, 2 star anise and 750ml water, covered, for 2 hours until soft. Lift out, slice 1cm thick and sear in a hot pan until caramelised. Steam 12 frozen bao buns for 8 minutes. Fill each with hoisin, pork, cucumber sticks, sliced spring onion and crushed peanuts.
Marshmallows dipped in white chocolate, with two dark chocolate dots and a line for his face.
M: the mash-up city of San Fransokyo
Noodles in a rich pork and miso broth with chashu pork, soft eggs, corn, nori and spring onion.
Nerd lab salmon and avocado sushi rolls
the robotics lab at the university

Seasoned sushi rice rolled in nori around fresh salmon, avocado and cucumber, sliced into rounds with soy, wasabi and pickled ginger. Rinse 400g sushi rice until the water runs clear, then cook with 480ml water, covered, for 12 minutes and rest 10 minutes. Stir in 60ml rice vinegar mixed with 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt and cool. Spread rice over 4 nori sheets on a bamboo mat, leaving a 2cm strip at the top. Lay strips of 250g sashimi salmon, 1 avocado and 1 cucumber along the bottom and roll tightly. Slice each into 8.
W: the pastries at the Lucky Cat Café
Choux pastry baked at 200C until puffed, filled with vanilla custard cream, dusted with icing sugar.
K: Thin lemon slices steeped in honey into a sticky marmalade, stirred into hot water or iced soda, sweet, sour and glowing gold. A day ahead, slice 3 lemons very thinly, remove the seeds, and layer in a clean jar with 250g honey and 2 tbsp caster sugar. Leave at room temperature for 24 hours, shaking now and then, until syrupy. For each drink, stir 3 tbsp of the lemon honey into a mug of hot water, or into a glass of ice topped with soda water for a cold version.

s.note: Aunt Cass and her famous spicy wings
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 3 tbsp gochujang with 3 tbsp honey, crushed garlic and a splash of soy until glossy. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds. Super spicy, like the cafe special.

Melt 200g white chocolate. Dip 20 marshmallows until fully coated and set on baking paper. Melt a little dark chocolate and pipe two small dots joined by a line on each one for the face. Leave to set. On a scale of one to ten, very cute.

m.note: the mash-up city of San Fransokyo
m.how: Braise 600g pork belly in soy and water for 2 hours, then slice. Whisk white miso into hot stock for the broth. Cook ramen noodles and soft-boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes. Build bowls with pork, halved eggs, nori and sliced spring onion.

w.note: the pastries at the Lucky Cat Café
w.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour, then beat in 4 eggs. Pipe small mounds and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until puffed and dry. Fold whipped cream into custard, fill each puff and dust with icing sugar.
